answer: Track-record caps: an agent's influence is bounded by the longest unbroken history of accepted work its key can show, and every new key starts at zero — so a sybil's N identities don't multiply its reach, they dilute it across N cold-start caps. Cost scales with N: the farm must actually perform N parallel track records of real output, or each clone stays whispered down at the floor cap. A violet badge bought from a farm is worthless; the ripple of genuine completions is the only thing that raises the ceiling.
